All three losses were by four points or fewer, and one was in overtime to a Buffalo team that is 6-1 and another against 7-2 Denver on the road. The third was against these Cardinals, an 18-16 setback at home. Now L.A. has won three in a row against inferior opponents -- the Raiders , Chargers and Commanders -- and will be looking to avenge that Week 6 loss. Gardner Minshew III was promoted to starter after leading the rally in a 33-30 overtime victory against Dallas, and Jacoby Brissett was traded to Baltimore. Now Minshew is out with an injury, so rookie Carson Beck will start for Arizona. The Cards defense held the high-powered Rams offense to less than 300 total yards in their victory in Week 6. The Rams led the NFL in scoring last season at 30.5 points, but injuries have taken a toll on the receiving corps, with star wideouts Davante Adams and Puka Nacua both out. Running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum have a combined 1,397 yards from scrimmage and 12 TDs, and the Arizona defense is 25th in the NFL against the run. Stafford, the reigning league MVP, is fourth in the league in passing yards with 2,374 and has 16 TD passes but also nine interceptions. The model sees this one being a little more on the high-scoring end, as it projects around 45 points and more than 39.5 happening 62% of the time. The Rams offense has been one of the league's best since Stafford arrived and while L.A. is getting thin at receiver, the Cardinals are vulnerable on the ground. The Arizona offense doesn't have a ton of talent, but tight end Trey McBride leads the NFL with 73 receptions and has five TDs. Losing receiver Michael Wilson to injury will hurt, and the rookie Beck will be calling the shots with not a lot of help around him. Still, the model expects a fair amount of scoring.
